The eleven ratings for Indutrade
Indutrade (INDT-SE) · Investment memo · 23 October 2026

Indutrade: both compounding engines have restarted and the earnings can be counted on, but over the next 18 months the yield-driven multiple, not the company's delivery, will set the return

Investment Analyst, 23 October 2026, written on the day of the Q3 2026 report. Share price SEK 262 to 267 before today's reaction; two-year-forward P/E about 22x. Margins are on the company's EBITA basis and EPS is on an adjusted basis (acquired-intangible amortisation added back) unless labelled otherwise; the end notes explain the bases.

The bottom line

  1. The earnings case is strong and dependable. Both of Indutrade's growth engines, acquisitions and organic growth, restarted in 2026, and adjusted EPS should compound at about 11.5% a year to 2030 on mechanics the company has demonstrated across three cycles.
  2. The return depends on the multiple, and our fair multiple is 24 to 25x, not the guideline 32.67x. At 24 to 25x the expected total shareholder return is about +36% over 18 months and +57% over three years. With no re-rating at all, earnings and dividends alone deliver about +18% and +37%.
  3. The guideline multiple's +78% is not supported by the research. Reaching 32.67x needs the yield regime to reverse and the discount to peers to close at the same time, which we put at below one in five.
  4. The skew changes with the horizon. It is positive for the next two prints, negative for the four quarters from Q2 2027, and positive again beyond 2028. The July 2027 print is the test.
  5. Interest rates are the one variable to watch. A Riksbank pause would turn a solid earnings case into a re-rating case; a hike into a Swedish slowdown would turn it into a sideways year with a floor near 20x. Because rates drive both the earnings bear case and the multiple bear case, the lower tail is fat.
  6. The practical stance: own the earnings growth, and size the position for the possibility that the cohort de-rates while the company delivers.

#0 Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

  1. 1

    Indutrade is the largest and lowest-margin of the four proven Swedish serial compounders, and its growth formula is mechanical. The group owns more than 220 technical-trading and niche-manufacturing companies, organised in 35 segments and five business areas and overseen by a 24-person head office. Since the 2005 listing the formula has been to buy 6 to 7% of sales each year at 5 to 8x EBITA from family sellers, to add 3 to 4% organic growth, to hold the EBITA margin at 14 to 15% through cycles, and never to issue equity or buy back shares. That formula compounded EPS at about 15% a year to 2023.

    The formula stalled in 2024 to 2025. Organic growth fell to −2%, the contribution of acquisitions to growth halved to 4 to 5%, selling, general and administrative costs (SG&A) had been built for volume that never came, and a concealed SEK 125m overrun on a UK project emerged. EPS fell two years running and the shares halved from SEK 330 to 170.

  2. 2

    Today's Q3 report confirmed, for a second consecutive quarter, that both engines have restarted. Growth, margin, costs and deals all moved the right way at once (tiles below): EBITA beat consensus by 1.2%, organic orders rose 6%, and Infrastructure & Construction returned to organic growth a year before our model assumed.

    The investment case rests on a proven formula returning, not on a new story. About four-fifths of the forecast rests on strengths that Indutrade has shown across three prior cycles; the remaining fifth rests on repeating this year's cost discipline and sustaining the organic growth rate when comparisons harden from Q2 2027.

  3. 3

    Our forecasts are not heroic: they sit level with consensus for 18 months and above it from 2028. We forecast revenue growth of about 9% a year and an EBITA margin that rises to levels above any year in the company's history. The dividend rises about 10% a year, and leverage drifts down to about 1.25x net debt to EBITDA while the deal programme funds itself. Consensus is about right for the next 18 months and 3 to 6% too low from 2028, because brokers model completed deals only.

  4. 4

    Over the next 18 months the multiple will matter more to the share price than the earnings, and the research puts the fair multiple at 24 to 25x, not the guideline 32.67x. Yields set the level of the cohort's multiple, and the cohort's multiple sets Indutrade's. The yield regime turned adverse in October: the US ten-year yield reached 5.1%, the Riksbank and the European Central Bank (ECB) are leaning toward rate hikes, and Addtech has already de-rated to 18.5x EV/EBITA.

    Indutrade's 15 to 20% discount to Lifco, Addtech and Lagercrantz is set by company facts that management has chosen not to change: lower organic growth, an 18% ROCE against the peers' 20%, and an 8.6x median entry multiple against their 6.7x. All four sets of research place the fair multiple at 24 to 25x. The guideline of 32.67x from Viewforth's Phases rule is the stock's ten-year 90th percentile, reached only at the 2021 peak on 16% organic growth and falling rates.

  5. 5

    At our fair multiple the expected return is about +36% over 18 months and +57% over three years, and earnings and dividends alone deliver +18% and +37%. The 18-month return is about 30% annualised and the three-year return about 18% annualised. The earnings leg is the dependable part of the return; the multiple leg is a wager on yields. At the guideline multiple the Financial Analyst's model gives +78% to December 2027 and +104% to June 2029, but two-thirds of those returns come from the multiple.

  6. 6

    Four judgements move the shares, and a two-turn change in the multiple outweighs any single earnings judgement.

    1. 2027 organic growth. The base case is 3.5%. Each point of organic growth is worth about SEK 185m of EBITA and 3.4% of EPS, and a relapse to 0% would cut EPS by 12%.
    2. The deal engine. The base case is SEK 2.3 to 2.6bn of acquired sales a year. A return to the 2025 pace would cost 2% of EPS a year, compounding.
    3. Cost discipline. Half a point on the ratio of SG&A to sales is worth 3.5% of EPS.
    4. The multiple. Each two-turn move in the multiple is worth 11% of the share price.

    Three other variables are noise around these four: a 5% move in the krona is worth 2.2% of EPS, 100 basis points on interest rates 1.2%, and a repeat control failure (a one-off charge of SEK 125 to 250m) 2.5 to 5%.

  7. 7

    The skew is positive for the next two prints, negative for the four quarters from Q2 2027, and positive again beyond 2028. The comparison bases, interest rates and the krona explain each turn (figure). The lower tail of the combined outcome is fat because one variable, interest rates, drives both the earnings bear case and the multiple bear case.

  8. 8

    We differ from the market in four places: we are below it on 2027 interest costs and the July 2027 print, and above it on cash conversion and on earnings from 2028. The market's figure for the interest line comes from the only published model, which still has 2027 net financial items falling to SEK −330m on rate cuts that are not coming; we have SEK −485m, a difference worth about 3% of EPS. Consensus assumes about 5% organic growth in the July 2027 print against a +5% comparison. The brokers quote cash conversion of 63 to 69% of EBITA, which is equivalent to about 100% of reported net income after leases. We agree with the market that the discount to peers is earned and will not close inside 18 months, that the recovery is cyclical with structural Life Science and energy strands inside it, and on the margin path.

  9. 9

    The setup is not the ideal configuration, but a real asymmetry exists in three specific places.

    What weakens the setup

    • There is no guidance to raise.
    • There is no narrative novelty before a 2028 Capital Markets Day.
    • 70% of analysts already rate the shares a Buy, and sell-side momentum is at a two-year peak.
    • The share price is 19% above its 200-day average after a 45% rebound.

    Where the asymmetry lies

    • The out-years: consensus has not booked deals that are not yet announced.
    • A Riksbank pause would lift the whole cohort's multiple, and Indutrade's multiple moves 1.2 times as much as the cohort's.
    • The earnings bear case (flat EPS in 2027) still does not break the 14% margin floor, the dividend or the deal programme.
  10. 10

    Five markers will test the case, and the July 2027 print matters most. The Q4 report on 27 January comes first; the Riksbank decisions in November and February set the cohort's multiple; and EUR/SEK and the quarterly run-rate of acquired sales are the continuous checks (calendar below).

Scorecard

#1 Tailwinds in the operating environment; absence of headwinds

Demand has turned up broadly, with orders leading sales, so the external environment is a moderate tailwind for earnings; rising yields make the same environment a headwind for the multiple.

Evidence. Demand has turned from a four-quarter trough, when organic growth ran between −4% and 0% from Q2 2025 to Q1 2026, to two consecutive quarters of +5% organic growth. Orders lead sales, breadth widened in Q3, the leading indicators agree, and the cost and currency backdrop has eased. The table sets out each indicator.

Inference. The turn is early-cycle, order-led and broad, and it runs against the easiest comparisons of the cycle. Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 both printed 0% organic growth, so the base effect alone will carry above-normal reported growth through Q1 2027.

About 40% of sales (Life Science, electrification, water and data-centre cooling) sits on structural drivers that will run regardless of the cycle. The other 60% rides a short-cycle recovery that Bernstein's indicator places six quarters into an upswing that lasts fourteen quarters on average. Visibility on demand is therefore two to three quarters, not two years.

So what. The model's organic growth inputs (4.5% in H2 2026, 3.5% in 2027 and 3% thereafter) are at or below what the current run-rate and the PMI lead imply, which is the right place to be when the macro regime has just turned. The external environment is a moderate tailwind for earnings and, through yields, a headwind for the multiple.

Strongest counter-case. The new interest-rate regime is the headwind. Sweden is among the most rate-sensitive economies in Europe. The Riksbank, at 1.75%, is leaning toward 2.25 to 2.50% by mid-2027, and the ECB toward 2.75 to 3.00%. DNB's strategy desk counts a broadening of profit warnings among Swedish mid-caps.

The industrial data are mixed. German factory orders fell 10.6% in August and German automotive orders 13% in September; Rothschild Redburn expects no meaningful European construction recovery before 2027; and EU steel output fell 6% in September. Two-thirds of Indutrade is cyclical, and half of that cyclical part is early-cyclical.

Addtech and Lifco, the two most compounder-like peers, printed organic growth of +1% and +1.6% on hard comparisons. Indutrade's own prints will look like that from Q2 2027 if its recovery is only a base effect.

What would change my view. Upward: the PMI holding above 52 into Q1 2027, book-to-bill staying above 100% for a fourth consecutive quarter, or a Riksbank pause. Downward: the PMI falling back below 50, which leads organic growth down by two to five quarters, or any quarter of organic growth below 2%.

Versus the market. The sell-side and we agree that the turn is cyclical with structural strands inside it. Retail investors and some brokers read it as a bounce; we read the breadth (five of five areas growing, construction positive and orders still ahead of sales) as a genuine turn. We are, however, more cautious than DNB on 2027: DNB carries about 5% organic growth through the hard Q2 2027 comparison, and we carry 3%.

Score: 58. A real, broad, order-led demand turn with structural strands inside it, set against a rates regime that has just turned against the cohort and a construction leg that has only just stopped falling.

#2 Internally-driven corporate change forces; absence of problems

The 2024 to 2025 reorganisation has restarted the deal engine as designed, and cost discipline is proven; management has not, however, raised its ambition, added an organic growth mechanism or strengthened governance after a real failure.

Evidence. The reorganisation was designed to double deal capacity without adding central bureaucracy. It replaced eight regional business areas with five sector business areas, then created 35 segments whose leaders both coach 6 to 8 companies and source deals from a mapped network of 1,500 candidates. It also added eight regional holding companies, AI screening of acquisition targets and a six-category portfolio model.

The first full year under the new structure has produced the step-up in deals it was designed for. By late October, 13 deals had added SEK 2.1bn of acquired annual sales, against SEK 1.3bn in all of 2025 and SEK 1.6bn in 2024. Three-quarters of the deals were sourced internally, the aggregate price of 1.22x sales matches the long-run median, and the acquired companies entered at EBITA margins of 17 to 19% against the group's 14 to 15%. The acquired contribution to EBITA growth is back at 8%, up from 4 to 5%.

Management has refreshed the layer beneath the chief executive more than at any time in his nine years in post, and has demonstrated cost discipline.

The cost record is concrete. About 200 roles were removed from demand-challenged units, four dilutive businesses with about SEK 200m of revenue were sold, and the UK managers were removed. Costs have now grown more slowly than sales for two quarters: in Q3, costs below gross profit rose about 11% against sales growth of 13%. S&P moved the outlook on its BBB− rating to positive.

Inference. The change forces form a coherent chain aimed at the one constraint that limits a compounder of this size, which is deal capacity, and they have begun to show in the numbers where they should show first. They are not transformational, for four reasons.

  1. The financial targets were reconfirmed, not raised. The chief executive refused to lift the 14% margin floor so that segment leaders can keep buying high-return, lower-margin trading companies.
  2. The organic engine has no new mechanism beyond coaching.
  3. Insider ownership is weak. The chief executive holds shares worth about one to two years' salary and made no open-market purchases in 2025.
  4. The board declined to add an internal audit function after a concealment that ran undetected for several quarters across 220 companies.

So what. The internal change supports the historical formula (10 to 13% EBITA growth when organic growth is 3 to 4%) running again at a slightly larger scale; it does not support a margin journey toward Lifco or Lagercrantz. The model's acquired-sales path, SEK 2.3bn in 2027 rising to SEK 3.0bn in 2030, sits inside the demonstrated range and does not require management's ambition of 20 to 30 deals a year.

Strongest counter-case. Three problems remain live.

  1. The UK project companies still drag on Technology & Systems Solutions. The area grew only 2% organically in Q3 with its margin down year on year; management says there is no quick fix and is exiting hydrogen work to rebuild customer relationships.
  2. Deals are fewer and larger. Recent deals cost SEK 130 to 345m each against a historical median of SEK 75m, which raises the stakes per deal in a model that does no integration and would not fix a weak acquisition.
  3. The segment layer could deter sellers. A former Lifco head of acquisitions describes the segment layer as creeping centralisation that could deter the family sellers who choose Indutrade for its autonomy. The H1 deal count says this has not happened yet, but the segment layer that sources deals is the same layer that holds costs, so a stretched segment layer would weaken both.

What would change my view. Upward: a 2026 deal count of 18 or more at unchanged pricing, or a Technology & Systems Solutions margin above 14% by Q4. Downward: a quarter with no deals, a median all-in entry multiple above 9x, a second write-down like the UK one, or SG&A growing faster than sales in a quarter of positive organic growth.

Versus the market. The sell-side gives management a credibility score of 4.0 out of 5.0 and treats the deal step-up as the thesis; retail investor forums treat the missing internal audit function as a sign of a systemic problem. On control we are nearer the retail view, because a recurrence of SEK 100 to 300m in a quarter is plausible and the control gap is unchanged. On the deal engine we are nearer the sell-side.

Score: 60. A restored, self-funded deal engine and demonstrated cost discipline, aimed at the right constraint, with no raised ambition, no organic mechanism and no governance scaffolding added after a real failure.

#3 Value chain, industry structure, business model, financial profile, management

The industry structure is the most reliable part of the case, but Indutrade earns second-rank margins and returns within its cohort, and that gap justifies its valuation discount.

Evidence. Indutrade's end markets are thousands of local, specified, technically served niches. The top five serial acquirers hold under 5% of them, no customer is above 3% of Indutrade's sales, the ten largest subsidiaries make up 19% of the group, and competitors put return on capital before volume. The proof of that discipline is that gross margins rose through a seven-quarter volume decline across the cohort: at Indutrade from 34.6% in 2023 to 35.8% now, at Addtech by 330 basis points from 2022 to 2025, at Lagercrantz to above 39%, and at Bufab for twelve consecutive quarters.

The group is resilient and lightly capitalised. Sales fell only 7.5% in 2008 to 2009, and the quarterly EBITA margin has never been below 13.3%. Capex is 1.6% of sales. Financial net debt excluding leases is about 1.2x EBITDA, with SEK 6.3bn of undrawn facilities and an investment-grade rating.

The financial profile is second-rank within the cohort on every margin and return measure, as the table below shows. Cash conversion is the one outlier strength: about 100% of reported net income after leases, and above 130% of EBITA on the company's own measure for eleven consecutive quarters.

Management is disciplined, honest and continuity-minded. It has never issued equity, has held entry multiples at 5 to 8x and leverage at 1.1 to 1.7x, and has doubled the group in nine years. It called the UK failure "completely unacceptable", and it has chosen a 14% margin floor over a Lifco-style margin ambition.

Inference. Indutrade has two tiers of moat. At subsidiary level the moat consists of specification lock-in, local stock and application engineering, exclusive territories and a 40 to 42% share of proprietary products; it is real, and the gross margin that rose while volumes fell is the evidence.

At group level the moat is Indutrade's reputation as a permanent home for family businesses, which produces proprietary deal flow at 6 to 8x EBITA. That group-level moat is a process advantage that needs refuelling every year, and Indutrade pays more for it than its best peers: DNB puts Indutrade's median entry multiple for 2023 to 2025 at 8.6x against 6.6 to 6.8x for the peers. Redeye's split of the price (7x initially, 9x with maximum earn-outs) suggests that most of the gap reflects earn-out structure and deal size rather than lost auctions.

The industry structure justifies, with confidence, a flat 35.5% gross margin and a 14% margin floor in the model. The value chain's one fragile link is the acquisition market, which is effectively Indutrade's supply chain. New Nordic platforms and private equity have pushed multiples for larger deals from 4 to 6x toward 8 to 10x, while the market for deals below EUR 20m, where Indutrade mostly buys, has held.

So what. The model assumes parity in end markets (no share gain and no price war), stable channel economics with a slow drift in the standardised trading minority, mix-driven margin improvement of 10 to 20 basis points a year, and an explicit sensitivity to entry multiples. The 15 to 20% valuation discount to the proven peers is earned by the return gap, and management does not intend to close the gap by changing the model.

Strongest counter-case. Digital disintermediation could erode the technical-trading half of the group (58% of sales), through manufacturers selling direct and AI-assisted procurement. The company itself names disintermediation as a high competitive risk in its 2026 prospectus. An automation-channel expert interviewed in Q3 reports that distributors are passing on only 2 to 3% against cost inflation of 3 to 4%, now that restored product availability has returned bargaining power to customers.

The evidence so far is that specified components resist disintermediation and that the damage is confined to catalogue-type electronics in Technology & Systems Solutions. A bear case of 20 to 50 basis points of gross-margin erosion in the trading half over three years fits inside the 14% margin floor.

What would change my view. A fall of more than 30 basis points in the company-basis gross margin over two quarters without an input-cost shock to explain it, or evidence that realised entry multiples are moving above 9x all-in.

Versus the market. Consensus and we agree on all of this, and it is the most-discussed part of the narrative. The one point where we push back on the sell-side is cash conversion. DNB's 63% and Redeye's 69% are measured against EBITA and are equivalent to about 100% of net income, so the discount the sell-side attaches to "weaker cash conversion" is partly a definitional artefact.

Score: 62. A robustly supportive industry structure and a clean, self-funding, asset-light model run by disciplined management, let down by second-quartile returns and margins and by the price it pays per deal.

#4 Guidance conservatism, sell-side expectations, track record of delivery and upgrades

There is no guidance to beat and the estimate base has already been rebuilt; the conservatism that remains is structural, because brokers model only completed deals.

Evidence. Indutrade gives no numerical guidance for any period. Its through-cycle targets are sales growth of at least 10%, an EBITA margin of at least 14%, ROCE of at least 20%, net debt below 100% of equity and a payout of 30 to 50%. The targets were reconfirmed in November 2025 and have never been cut, and the margin floor was raised at each of the two previous Capital Markets Days, from 10% to 12% in 2018 and from 12% to 14% in 2022. In 2026 the company will narrowly miss the growth target, clear the margin floor by a full point and fall two points short of the ROCE target.

The sell-side record has three phases. Indutrade delivered strongly against consensus from 2021 to 2023. It then missed consensus in three of four quarters to Q1 2026, the largest miss being 14% on adjusted EBITA because of the UK write-down. Since then it has beaten consensus twice in a row, by 11 to 12% in Q2 and by about 1% in Q3, against a consensus that had already risen.

Expectations have been rebuilt. FY2027 consensus EPS has risen 6% in six months and FY2028 25% in twelve months; target prices are up 11% to a mean of SEK 285; and the share of Buy ratings is up 30 points to 70%. The three Holds (DNB at SEK 260, Pareto at 265 and Goldman Sachs at 261) rest on valuation, not on estimates; the Buys (Nordea at 322, and two restricted brokers at 290 and 295) rest on the compounding runway. On 5 October DNB cut its target with unchanged estimates, because the earnings yield had tightened against the ten-year euro swap rate.

Inference. With no guidance to beat or miss, there will be no company-led upgrade cycle. The tone of the quarterly report is the only forward signal, and it has been a reliable one-quarter lead. The estimate base is no longer depressed: estimates troughed in April, have since been rebuilt, and the share price has rewarded the turn.

The conservatism that remains is structural rather than cyclical. Brokers book completed deals only, so each acquisition announcement is a small upgrade, and the 5% FY2028 revenue growth in consensus is the visible symptom.

So what. The predictability of the forecasts rests on delivery against consensus rather than against any promise, and the setup is less favourable than it was six months ago. The one plausible change to the targets is a 15% margin floor at a 2028 Capital Markets Day. We put its probability at about 40%, conditional on 2027 printing a 15.0% margin, and such a change would confirm rather than surprise.

Strongest counter-case. In our favour: the misses were concentrated in cost absorption and one control failure, not in gross margin, cash or deal discipline. The company beats when volume arrives, because its cost base does not flex; with volume now arriving against easy comparisons, the next two prints are more likely to beat than to miss. Against us: the Hold brokers' targets equal the share price, and a yield-driven regime cuts targets while raising estimates, as DNB's cut on 5 October showed.

What would change my view. A Q4 print with organic growth above 5% and an underlying margin above 15.5% would turn the near-term nudge into upgrades of 3 to 5% and would move the Holds on estimates rather than valuation. A Q4 organic print below 3% would bring the expected July 2027 cut forward.

Versus the market. Consensus FY2026 EBIT of SEK 5,127m is now achievable, and our updated figure is level with it. Consensus FY2027 is about 1 to 3% too high at the pre-tax line, because of its interest assumption, and about right at EBITA. Consensus FY2028 is 3 to 6% too low. The market treats the two beats as a restored record; we treat them as two of the minimum three needed.

Score: 50. No guidance to raise, targets that are floors already exceeded, a rebuilt rather than depressed estimate base and a sell-side that is now 70% Buy, offset by two consecutive beats and a structural under-modelling of future deals.

#5 Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost control and feedback loops

Operating leverage follows a simple rule, about one-third of a point of margin for each point of organic growth above about 2%, and with mix that rule carries the margin to records; the downside is wider than the upside because costs are cut only with a lag.

Evidence. Operating leverage is the largest single mechanism in the forecast, and it can be written as a rule: the group EBITA margin moves about one-third of a point for each point of organic growth above or below a break-even of about 2%. The rule holds because the cost base below gross profit (about SEK 7bn, or 21 to 22% of sales, mostly the people in 220 companies) grows at wage inflation regardless of volume, while each additional krona of organic sales carries 35.5 öre of gross profit.

The rule fits three periods. In Q2 2026, organic growth of +5% lifted the margin by 100 basis points. Over 2024 to 2025, organic growth of about −2% over two years cut the margin by 120 basis points. In Q3 2026, organic growth of +5% lifted the margin by 70 basis points; the shortfall against the rule came from project mix at Process, Energy & Water.

The other levers are small or defensive, as the table shows.

Four reinforcing loops drive the compounding: deal sourcing, the acquisition arithmetic (buying at 8 to 8.5x EBITA all-in while the shares trade at 17 to 20x EV/EBITA), operating leverage converting to cash, and mix. Life Science earns an 18.2% margin and acquired companies 17 to 19%, so mix lifts the group margin without any operating improvement.

Inference. Revenue growth produces outsized profit growth through two channels that are running together for the first time since 2023. First, organic EBITA grows at about twice the rate of organic sales while the pre-built cost base is absorbed, a ratio that fades to 1.5x by 2028. Second, acquired EBITA enters at margins 2 to 4 points above the group's.

Three balancing loops cap the compounding rate at 9 to 11% EBITA growth from 2028, rather than the 12 to 15% of 2017 to 2023. The first is scale, since each deal is only 0.4% of sales. The second is acquisition pricing, since each extra turn of multiple on SEK 2.7bn of annual deployment costs about SEK 30m of EBITA a year, cumulatively. The third is complexity and control.

So what. The model carries the leverage rule explicitly (about +40 basis points of margin in 2026 and 2027, +20 in 2028 and +10 thereafter), a flat gross margin, mix of +10 to 20 basis points a year, and no cost programme.

The rule is asymmetric, and the asymmetry matters. On the way up, operating leverage arrives within the quarter because the capacity is already paid for. On the way down, costs follow with a two-to-four-quarter lag because the chief executive will not cut lean trading companies indiscriminately. The range of margin outcomes over any twelve-month window is therefore wider on the downside: a relapse to 0% organic growth in 2027 would take the margin to about 14.3% rather than 15.0%.

Strongest counter-case. Indutrade's operating leverage is larger than its peers' because its gross margin is lower and its trading share higher. That is a disadvantage in a downturn, as 2024 to 2025 proved, and it is also why Indutrade has the most to gain now.

The loops share one cause. The volume that produces operating leverage is also the volume that makes owners willing to sell and keeps acquired companies on their earn-out plans. (A positive earn-out remeasurement, such as the SEK 208m booked in 2025, is bad news dressed as income, because it means acquired companies fell short of their plans.) A relapse in volume would therefore hit both loops at once.

What would change my view. SG&A growing faster than sales for two quarters of positive organic growth (the 2024 pattern); the gross margin slipping toward 35% in the Swedish import-and-resell subsidiaries as the weak krona raises landed costs with a two-to-four-quarter repricing lag; or a realised all-in entry multiple above 9x.

Versus the market. DNB's central thesis since July is the same operating-leverage story, but nobody on the sell-side states the rule or its asymmetry. The market has not priced two drags: the weak krona's effect on purchasing costs, worth 10 to 20 basis points of gross margin in 2027, and the fact that, with rates rising, the lines below EBITA will subtract about a point a year from EPS growth rather than adding one.

Score: 62. Demonstrated two-way operating leverage, margin-defending pricing, a mechanical and self-funded acquisition loop and a neutral balance sheet, with no cost lever to pull if volume relapses and a return per deal compressed by the price paid.

#6 Forecast financials; scope for double-digit growth and for higher growth and margins than the past

Our forecasts deliver double-digit EBITA and EPS growth and record margins from mechanics the company has already demonstrated; they do not require faster revenue growth than in the past.

Revenue growth is built from three parts: 6 to 6.5% from acquisitions, 3 to 3.5% organic (about 2 points of it from price) and zero from currency. The acquired part assumes SEK 2.3bn of annual sales bought in 2027, rising to SEK 3.0bn in 2030, at 1.2x sales; including earn-out settlements, that costs SEK 2.65bn to 3.3bn of cash a year. The margin path combines operating leverage, mix and the recovery of the two weak business areas: Technology & Systems Solutions from 13.5% to 15% by 2028, and Infrastructure & Construction from 12% to 13%.

Below EBITA, amortisation of acquired intangibles grows from SEK 656m to about SEK 1.0bn; net financial items rise in absolute terms as rates rise and net debt stays near SEK 10bn; tax is 23.3 to 23.5% of reported pre-tax profit; and the share count stays at 364.3m. Free cash flow after capex and leases, about SEK 2.9bn rising to SEK 4.9bn (96 to 105% of reported net income), funds the dividends and the whole acquisition programme. The model's working-capital treatment overstates year-end net debt by a cumulative SEK 1 to 2bn by 2030, so the true leverage path is nearer 1.25x than the 1.4x the model shows.

Today's Q3 print landed slightly above the model's Q3 inputs: revenue grew 13% against the 11% assumed, and EBITA was SEK 1,358m against about SEK 1,325m. Q4 will also carry the October deals. We therefore lift FY2026 revenue growth to 9.1% and the FY2026 EBITDA margin to 17.8%, and FY2027 revenue growth to 9.5%. The lift adds about 1% to 2026 and 2027 EPS, to about SEK 10.3 and SEK 11.7, and brings FY2026 EBITA level with consensus.

Inference. The forecasts answer the topic's three questions clearly.

The composition of growth is identical to history; what differs now is that both engines are running at once.

So what. The forecasts rest on strengths the company demonstrably has and do not require any decision that management has refused to take. Against consensus, our revenue was 1% below for 2026 before today's lift and is level after it; our EBITA is level in 2026 and 2027; our pre-tax profit is 4 to 5% below in 2027 because of higher interest costs; and our EBITA is 5% above in 2028.

The range of outcomes is narrow for 2026 and wider for 2027. Our 2026 adjusted EPS falls within ±4% of the forecast with 70% probability. Our 2027 adjusted EPS ranges from SEK 10.3 in the bear case, with EBITA flat at about SEK 5.1bn, to SEK 12.6 in the bull case, with EBITA of SEK 6.2bn.

Strongest counter-case. Three assumptions carry most of the weight. First, organic growth must hold at 3.5% through the hard comparisons of 2027, which the company has not yet demonstrated in this cycle (it is one quarter short). Second, the deal count must hold at 15 to 19 a year at the 2026 average size; the 2024 to 2025 stall shows that the count can halve when the organisation is distracted. Third, the SG&A ratio must drift down rather than up. The recovery of the two weak areas, worth 20 to 30 basis points of group margin over 2027 to 2028, is the only piece that rests on something not yet shown, and it is small and late.

What would change my view. The thresholds in #2 and #5, plus 2027 free cash flow after leases below 90% of reported net income; a 2022-style inventory build would halve a year's cash flow without touching EPS.

Versus the market. The model and the two adjusted-basis brokers, DNB and Nordea, are within 2% of each other in all three years from 2026 to 2028. Our difference from them has a consistent shape: slightly below for 18 months, and above thereafter. The reported-basis brokers (Pareto at SEK 8.46 and Goldman Sachs at 8.71) should be compared with the model's EPS less about SEK 2.0 a share.

Score: 62. Double-digit EBITA and EPS compounding from an undemanding base to a record margin, built from demonstrated mechanics and self-funded, but at a revenue growth rate below the company's own history and with a 2027 that depends on one cyclical variable.

#7 Scope for upgrades to guidance, sell-side estimates and the narrative over 6 to 12 months

Upgrades over the next two prints will be small and mechanical, July 2027 is where consensus is exposed to a cut, and the structural upgrade lies in 2028, where the share price does not yet look.

Evidence. The next five reports are dated, and each faces a known comparison base.

  • Q4 2026, 27 January 2027: the easiest base of the cycle (0% organic growth; a 13.3% reported margin after the write-down, 14.9% underlying). The report brings the dividend proposal, where SEK 3.30 or 3.40 would each meet expectations, and the 2026 deal count.
  • Q1 2027, April: a base of 0% organic growth and a 13.3% margin; the first report under the new finance chief.
  • Q2 2027, July: a hard base of +5% organic growth, a 14.7% margin and +8% orders.
  • Q3 and Q4 2027: today's 15.3% margin and the Q4 2026 print.

Three other inputs will move estimates mechanically. The three deals announced in the week of 19 to 23 October (Euromed with SEK 230m of sales, Sinmed with 130m and Schraner with 90m) add about 1.3% to 2027 sales, which models of completed deals will now book. Currency translation at EUR/SEK 11.1 to 11.2 adds about 1% to estimates; DNB already took it on 9 October. FactSet rolls its base year in January, which will remove the "+42%" artefact and reset headline 2026 EPS growth to the like-for-like 17 to 24%.

Inference. Company guidance offers nothing to raise. For sell-side estimates, we assign probabilities event by event (figure). Q4 2026 is the likeliest upgrade, with a 45% probability, worth 1 to 3% on 2027 from deals and currency. Q2 2027 is the likeliest cut, with a 40 to 45% probability, because consensus carries about 5% organic growth into that quarter against a +5% base, and a 2% print at a 15% margin would take 2 to 3% off 2027 EPS. Net over 12 months, FY2027 estimates should hold within ±3%, and FY2028 estimates should be upgraded by 3 to 6% (probability about 65%) as deals are booked.

The narrative ahead is a sequence of confirmations of a known model, none of them novel: a margin above 15% for a full year, ROCE back toward 20%, Life Science sales toward SEK 10bn, a record deal year, an S&P upgrade to BBB within 18 months on the positive outlook, and the new chief financial officer completing the handover. The first plausible novelty is a 2028 Capital Markets Day.

So what. The revision stream is small and front-loaded, and then it is tested. The favourable gap between our numbers and the market's lies in 2028 and beyond. There, the sell-side's own M&A scenarios (DNB's SEK 281 with 7% acquired growth; Redeye's 18 deals a year to 2034) agree with us, while their base-case numbers do not. A gap between published numbers and published beliefs closes slowly.

Strongest counter-case. In our favour: the near-term upgrades could be larger than we assume if Q4 repeats the Q3 pattern (organic growth of 5% and a margin above 15% on the weakest base) and the deal count reaches 16 to 18, because the Holds would then have to move on estimates. Against us: revision breadth is already at its two-year peak, one- and three-month revisions have flattened to +1%, and a yield-driven regime cuts targets without cutting estimates, so even a clean upgrade stream may not move the share price.

What would change my view. Organic growth of 6% or more in Q4 with a 15.5% margin, which would make the upgrades 3 to 5%; a Riksbank path that stops at 2.00%, which would remove most of our difference from consensus on the interest line; or EUR/SEK at 10.8 by mid-2027, a 2 to 3% translation cut that nobody has modelled.

Versus the market. Over the next 12 months the market's blind spots are mostly on the downside: the interest line, the July 2027 test, the krona's forecast recovery, and the finding that quarterly dispersion widens in the first year of a recovery. Beyond 12 months they are on the upside: deals, cash conversion and SEK 6bn of balance-sheet capacity.

Score: 52. Small, mechanical near-term upgrades from deals and currency, a real test in July 2027 where consensus is exposed, and a structural upgrade stream that lives in 2028 where the share price does not yet look.

#8 Current momentum: guidance, sell-side, narrative, technicals, and peers

Momentum is strong on every measure the dashboard tracks, but the leading measure, revision breadth, has flattened, and the cohort's multiple is moving the other way.

Evidence. The dashboard rates sell-side momentum A, technical momentum B and valuation C; the narrative has also turned.

Peers that reported in the past fortnight split into two groups (table). OEM International, Bufab and Addtech all printed record margins (16.5%, 15.6% and 16.7% respectively), yet Addtech was still corrected to 18.5x EV/EBITA in October.

Inference. Momentum is strong in every dimension the dashboard measures, and it has plateaued in the dimension that leads, revision breadth. The stock's correlation with its peer basket has fallen through 2026, from about 0.7 to about 0.5; the basket now explains 19 to 26% of the stock's daily variance against 47% in 2024 to 2025, and beta is above 1.2. That combination is the signature of a stock re-pricing on its own events inside a sector that moves on yields.

Within the cohort, the short-cycle and trading-heavy names (OEM, Bufab and Beijer Ref) have the operating momentum and the A ratings, while the two purest compounders (Addtech and Lifco) face hard comparisons and softening narratives. Indutrade sits with the first group on operations and with the second group on how its multiple is set.

So what. Momentum favours the next two prints and says nothing about July 2027. The share price is at a 52-week high, 70% of analysts rate the shares a Buy, and the Hold targets equal the price, so a miss like the one in Q1 2026 would cost 10 to 15% quickly. The 45% rebound after Q2 shows how sensitive the shares are in both directions.

Strongest counter-case. The cohort's momentum is diverging from its multiple. OEM's multiple fell from 25x to 18x in four months this year on fund outflows while its earnings rose, and Addtech corrected in October on an in-line quarter. Strong operating momentum inside a de-rating cohort has historically produced sideways share prices: Lagercrantz fell 20% in a month in early 2022 despite double-digit earnings growth.

What would change my view. Three-month revision breadth turning negative; or the price closing below its 50-day average (about SEK 252) on volume after a clean print, which would signal that the yield channel has taken over.

Versus the market. The market reads A-rated momentum as a reason to own the shares. We read it as fully reflected in the price for the next 18 months, with the next leg dependent on delivery in July 2027 and on yields.

Score: 68. Sell-side momentum at a two-year peak, a share price at its highs, the narrative restored and short-cycle peers printing strongly, with the leading edge (revision breadth) already flat and the cohort's multiple moving the other way.

#9 Riskiness and simplicity of forecasts and expectations

The earnings can be forecast with confidence, but the 18-month return cannot: the swing in the multiple is about twice the swing in earnings, and interest rates drive both.

Evidence. The case is simple in mechanism and diffuse in source. The mechanism is two engines and a margin rule. Every link from the targets to EPS is disclosed, and acquisitions are announced deal by deal with sales and often margin, which makes the deal stream the best-disclosed driver in the cohort. The sources of earnings are diffuse: 220 companies, 30 countries, no customer above 3% of sales, and 80% of sales outside Sweden.

The level of earnings is therefore very predictable: the quarterly EBITA margin has never been below 13.3%, and sales fell only 7.5% in 2009. The growth of earnings, by contrast, depends on three throughput variables that move together: organic volume, the deal count and the SG&A ratio. All three turned down together in 2024 to 2025 and back up together in 2026.

Quarterly noise is 5 to 10% of EBITA, from earn-out remeasurements, project write-downs, currency and project timing, and the noise widens rather than narrows in the first year of a recovery as business areas diverge. The company does not disclose the split of growth between price and volume, SG&A by area, the multiple paid per deal, or anything on internal control between events.

Inference. We rank the risks to the share price by materiality and suddenness (table). The largest, a de-rating of the cohort on yields, would take 15 to 25% off the price with no change in earnings; it builds slowly, can be tracked through the ten-year euro swap rate and the Riksbank, and is already live. A short-seller attack is a real risk because Indutrade shares the features that attackers cite: acquired intangibles at about 45% of assets, earn-outs, no internal audit function, a thin head office and a recent concealment.

The forecast has four requirements: organic growth at or above 2% (the break-even in the margin rule), a deal count of 15 or more a year at the 2026 deal size, SG&A growing more slowly than sales, and no step-up in entry multiples.

The downside arithmetic is sobering. A fair trough multiple of 17 to 18x two-year-forward EPS gives SEK 195 to 210, about 25% below today. A crash multiple of 15.3x on EPS 15% lower gives SEK 150 to 170, 35 to 40% below today, which matches the brokers' bear cases and the 2025 low.

So what. The earnings can be forecast and the return cannot. Over 18 months, the multiple's plausible range of 18x to 27x (about ±20%) is about twice the earnings variance, and the multiple is correlated with the earnings through rates. The right approach is therefore to model the case with confidence at the annual group level, to judge it quarter by quarter, and not to buy on the forecast alone. The simplicity of the case is high; the simplicity of the perimeter is low; and sector and cyclical risk is high, with abundant precedent.

Strongest counter-case. Diversification is the defence that the precedents reward. The base rate of a diversified, unlevered Nordic compounder failing outright is near zero. The earnings bear case does not break the margin floor, the dividend or the deal programme, and the balance sheet lets the company buy through a downturn at better prices, although sellers tend to withdraw in recessions. The two biggest sentiment risks, yields and short-sellers, are sector-wide and are already partly reflected in a multiple at the 29th percentile of its five-year range.

What would change my view. A short-seller note on any member of the cohort; the ten-year euro swap rate rising another 50 basis points; cumulative write-downs above SEK 250m; or two quarters of book-to-bill below 100%.

Versus the market. The sell-side treats dispersion as having narrowed after Q2; the evidence says dispersion widens in the first year of a recovery. Retail investors are more alert to the control risk than institutions are. Nobody in the research files states the correlation between the earnings bear case and the multiple bear case, and that correlation is what makes the lower tail fat.

Score: 45. A simple, well-disclosed mechanism inside a wide perimeter, with three correlated drivers, meaningful unguided quarterly noise, and a share price whose 18-month variance is dominated by a yield-driven cohort multiple with severe sector precedents.

#10 Where the stock is in its lifecycle

On earnings the stock is in early reinforcing; its multiple is held back by a cohort that is stalling on yields, and the Q2 2027 print decides the next phase.

Evidence. Since early 2025 the stock has passed through four phases. It stalled in 2025, when the discount to Lagercrantz reached a record 20%. It collapsed from January to May 2026, when the two-year-forward P/E fell to 18.4x, a five-year low. It bottomed as orders turned positive in Q1 2026, the restructuring produced deals and the finance chief was replaced. It turned up on the Q2 beat, rising 45% in three months as the multiple returned to about 22x. Today's print is a second confirming quarter, with margin, orders, cash flow, deals and the weakest area all moving the right way.

The dashboard's rule places the starting phase at "Reinforcing". Four facts argue against a fuller reading: the multiple has recovered only to its ten-year median; the cohort's multiple is contracting on yields; there is no guidance or narrative novelty to carry a broadening; and this company's multiple has historically peaked one to three quarters after the first positive organic quarter.

Inference. On fundamentals the stock has moved from turning up into early reinforcing: two consecutive quarters of delivery against consensus, both engines running, estimates rising and a record deal year. On the share price and the multiple it is in a different phase. The cohort's multiple is stalling under the yield regime, so Indutrade's delivery is being rewarded through a narrower discount rather than a higher level.

The accurate placement is therefore "early reinforcing on earnings, with the multiple held back by the sector". The thesis is being confirmed but not broadened, because the broadening steps (a margin ambition, an organic growth mechanism, a lower entry multiple) are steps that management has declined. The next phase transition is dated: in Q2 2027, reinforcing either continues, with organic growth of 3% or better against +5% and a margin above 15%, or it stalls.

So what. The phase supports a multiple between the ten-year median and the defendable band, not the peak-delivery band. It supports owning the earnings growth. It also argues for sizing the position for the possibility that the cohort de-rates while the company delivers, which is the modal outcome in the sector's history of rising-yield regimes.

Strongest counter-case. This cycle is gentler (5% organic growth, against 12 to 16% in 2010, 2017 and 2021), which could mean a longer, lower ramp in which the multiple does not peak early. And if yields turn, a stock two quarters into a confirmed recovery, with a record margin and a record deal year, is exactly the kind of stock that re-rates fastest. The 2024 precedent shows how far the stock travels when delivery and rates align: it reached 27 to 30x in July to September 2024 on a Q2 beat and falling rates.

What would change my view. Toward "reinforcing and broadening": a third beat in January with a deal count of 17 or more, plus a Riksbank pause. Toward "stalling": a July 2027 print below 3% organic growth, or revision breadth turning negative before then.

Versus the market. The dashboard's rule says "Reinforcing". The sell-side's actions (Holds on valuation, and targets trimmed on yield spreads while estimates rise) say "turning up inside a de-rating sector". We sit between the two, closer to the sell-side.

Score: 58. Early reinforcing on earnings after two confirming quarters, with the multiple's phase set by a cohort that is stalling on yields and no broadening step in management's plans.

#11 The fair multiple

The fair multiple for the next 18 months is 24 to 25x two-year-forward earnings, about 10% above today's 22x and far below the 32.67x guideline.

Evidence. Viewforth's Phases rule gives a guideline multiple of 32.67x two-year-forward earnings. That is the stock's ten-year 90th percentile (the "mania" band) and 50% above today's 21.8x. The ten-year bands are 15.3x (crash), 20.0x (conservative), 22.4x (median), 27.3x (defendable) and 32.7x (mania). Over five years the range is 17.9x to 38.2x, with a median of 25.1x and an interquartile range of 22.5x to 26.9x. Today's multiple sits at the 29th percentile of the five-year range and the 55th of the ten-year range.

History shows when high multiples occur. The stock traded above 30x only from March 2021 to January 2022, on 16% organic growth and rates near zero, peaking at 39.4x in July 2021. It touched 29 to 30x in mid-2024 on a Q2 beat with rates falling. It traded at 15 to 18x through 2016 to 2019, when the market valued it as a cyclical distributor tied to Swedish housing starts rather than as a compounder.

The sell-side's current anchors sit on both sides of our range. DNB uses 21.8x 2027 P/E and 17.3x 2027 EV/EBITA, a 20% discount to peers at 20 to 22x on its figures, and calculates a Gordon-growth "fair long-term P/E" of 18.5x at a 4% risk-free rate. Redeye's base case is 24 to 29x P/E for 2026 to 2027, with a historical-median argument for 34x. The Hold targets of SEK 260 to 265 imply about 22x, and Nordea's SEK 322 implies about 27x.

Inference. The guideline band belongs to a stock in peak delivery inside a cohort being re-rated upward. Indutrade is in early reinforcing inside a cohort being de-rated, and its discount to peers is earned by returns and margins that management does not intend to change. The fair multiple over the next 18 months therefore lies between the ten-year median and the defendable band. We place it at 24 to 25x, for three reasons:

  1. 24 to 25x is the five-year median.
  2. It is a modest premium to the ten-year median, justified by a record margin, both engines running, falling leverage and a likely S&P upgrade.
  3. It keeps a persistent discount to the peers' 26 to 28x.

The fair multiple is reachable without a change in the yield regime if the discount narrows another few points on delivery; it is not reachable if the cohort de-rates as it did in 2022. The other bands each need a specific trigger:

So what. Topic #12 should be read with 24 to 25x as the base multiple, and 27.3x and 20x as the bull and bear multiples. The guideline figure is the template's upper band, and we would not use it for sizing a position.

Strongest counter-case. Redeye makes the within-company argument. Every current multiple is 2 to 19% below the stock's own two- and five-year medians, and the historical median P/E of 34x implies SEK 342. A decentralised compounder with a 20-year record at scale, which has just restarted both engines and whose entry multiple on an EV-to-sales basis has not risen, has traded at 27 to 30x in every recovery since 2020. If the Riksbank pauses in November and the swap rate falls back, the cohort re-rates together, and Indutrade, with a beta above 1.2 to the cohort, re-rates most.

What would change my view. Up to 27x: two more beats and a Riksbank pause. Down to 20 to 22x: the ten-year euro swap rate another 50 basis points higher, a short-seller event in the cohort, or a July 2027 print below 3% organic growth.

Versus the market. The Hold brokers' implied 22x and DNB's long-term 18.5x sit below us; Nordea and Redeye sit above; the template sits far above. We are closest to the five-year median, which is also where the market itself has valued this stock, on average, through the last cycle.

Score: 55. Today's 22x is about 10% below our fair 24 to 25x and well inside the stock's own range, a modest but real valuation support, with the gap to the guideline 32.67x reflecting a phase the research does not find.

#12 Total shareholder return, Dupont framework

At our fair multiple the expected return is about +36% over 18 months and +57% over three years; the earnings leg is dependable, the multiple leg is a wager on yields, and the two legs are correlated on the downside.

Evidence. The Financial Analyst's model, starting from a share price of SEK 262.20, applies the guideline multiple at the 18-month column:

HorizonTSRAnnualisedValue per shareFrom dividendsFrom the multipleFrom earnings
18-month column, 31 December 2027+77.7%+62.2%SEK 466+2.7%+46.9%+19.1%
Three-year column, 30 June 2029+104.4%+30.5%SEK 536+4.3%+44.5%+38.4%

In the model, the earnings component is the growth in two-year-forward EPS from about SEK 12.3 today (SEK 262.2 divided by 21.3x on the model's measure) to about SEK 14.3 at December 2027 and about SEK 16.4 at June 2029. The multiple component is the move from 21.3x to 32.67x. The dividend component is SEK 3.40 for 2026 and a 40% payout in the years after.

Inference. Two-thirds of the model's return at both horizons comes from the multiple, and the research does not support that leg. The table below holds the model's earnings and dividends constant and varies only the multiple at the 18-month column.

The values per share include about SEK 7 of dividends over 18 months and about SEK 11 over three years; measuring from today's SEK 267 instead of SEK 262.20 lowers each return by about 2 points. At our fair multiple the 18-month return is about +36%, or about 30% annualised over the 14 months to the column date, and the three-year return is about +57%, or about 18% annualised. Earnings and dividends contribute about +21% and +43% of those returns, and the multiple +15% and +13%.

Combining the earnings range with the multiple range widens the outcomes. The earnings bear case (2027 EPS flat at about SEK 10.3) at 20x gives an 18-month return of roughly −5 to 0%; the earnings bull case (SEK 12.6) at 27x gives about +70%.

So what. The three drivers of the return, in order of dependability:

  1. The earnings leg (+19% to December 2027, +38% to June 2029) is the dependable component and rests on the two engines described in #5 and #6.
  2. The multiple leg is a wager that the cohort's yield-driven level does not fall and that Indutrade's discount narrows a little.
  3. The dividend is a 1.3% yield that grows 10% a year and will not be supplemented by buybacks.

The asymmetry is better over three years than over 18 months, because the earnings leg doubles while the multiple leg does not, and because the stream of deals not yet announced lands in 2028 to 2029.

Strongest counter-case. The two legs are correlated. The macro path that produces the earnings bear case, higher Swedish rates and a volume relapse in 2027, is the same path that takes the multiple to 20x. The joint bear case (about SEK 210 to 230, or −15 to −20%) is therefore more probable than the product of the two independent probabilities, and the joint bull case (above SEK 420) requires both yields and delivery to go right. Against that, a return of +18% over 14 months with no re-rating at all, on forecasts at or slightly below consensus, is a respectable floor for the base case.

What would change my view. The multiple thresholds in #11; a change in the earnings range from the judgements in #6; or any move by the company toward buybacks (none is expected) or toward using the SEK 6bn of balance-sheet capacity at a faster deal pace, which would add 2 to 3 points to annual EBITA growth and lift every row of the table.

Versus the market. The mean sell-side target of SEK 285 implies about +9% plus the dividend over twelve months, roughly our no-re-rating row compressed into one year. The Buy targets of SEK 290 to 322 sit between our fair and defendable rows. Nobody on the sell-side is near the template's SEK 466.

Score: 62. A base-case return of about +36% over 18 months and +57% over three years at a fair multiple, with an earnings-only floor of +18% and +37%, attractive in absolute terms but with its upside concentrated in a multiple the company does not control and its downside correlated across both legs.

#13 Summary conclusion on the business and its investment case

Indutrade is a proven compounding machine of the second rank that stalled for two years and has now shown the market, over two quarters, that both of its engines run again. The evidence is broad: organic growth at 5% with orders still ahead of sales, a record gross margin, costs growing more slowly than revenue, a record year of acquisitions at the company's historical price, the weakest business area back in growth, and cash flow up 20% with net debt falling in a quarter that included an acquisition. The forecasts that follow are not heroic: 9% revenue growth, a 15% margin in 2027 rising to a record 15.4%, EPS compounding at 11 to 13%, a dividend growing 10% a year and an acquisition programme that funds itself. They sit level with consensus for 18 months and above it beyond, and the company has done four-fifths of what they require in three previous cycles.

The investment case has one weakness, and it lies outside the company. Over the next 18 months the share price will be set more by the multiple the cohort carries than by Indutrade's delivery. The cohort's multiple is set by yields, which have turned against it, and Indutrade's own 15 to 20% discount within that multiple is earned by returns and margins that management has decided not to chase. The earnings can therefore be right and the share price wrong for a year, which is the modal outcome in the sector's history of rising-yield regimes. The same logic makes the template's guideline multiple of 32.67x inapplicable: the research places the fair multiple at 24 to 25x and the base-case return at about +36% over 18 months and +57% over three years, with an earnings-only floor of +18% and +37%.

The practical reading is clear. The next two prints are skewed positive, the July 2027 print is the test, the out-years are under-modelled, and the macro variable to watch is the Riksbank decision in November. A Riksbank pause would convert a solid earnings case into a re-rating case; a hike into a Swedish slowdown would convert it into a sideways year with a floor near 20x. The company's job is to keep doing what it did in Q2 and Q3. The investor's job is to decide how much of the multiple wager to take alongside the earnings that can reasonably be counted on.
